title: Mercy turns bitter into sweet
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 171
summary: The shabad opens by saying the Lord already dwells in the body-fortress, even though stubbornness cannot taste Him. It travels through mercy, Guru-centered sweetness, and the hard-hearted poison of the manmukh before ending where bitter becomes sweet in Sangat.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person close to sacred things but no longer tasting them. Kept close, it teaches that proximity is not enough; mercy and Shabad must soften the stubborn heart.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: ask for the mercy that turns nearness into tasted sweetness.

lines.gurmukhi: ਇਸੁ ਗੜ ਮਹਿ ਹਰਿ ਰਾਮ ਰਾਇ ਹੈ ਕਿਛੁ ਸਾਦੁ ਨ ਪਾਵੈ ਧੀਠਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: eis gaR meh har raam rai hai kichh saadh na paavai dheeThaa ||
lines.translation: Within this body-fortress is the Lord, the Sovereign Lord King, but the stubborn ones do not find the taste.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਦੀਨ ਦਇਆਲਿ ਅਨੁਗ੍ਰਹੁ ਕੀਆ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਚਖਿ ਡੀਠਾ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: har dheen dhiaal anugrahu keeaa har gur sabadhee chakh ddeeThaa ||1||
lines.translation: When the Lord, Merciful to the meek, showed His Mercy, I found and tasted it, through the Word of the Guru's Shabad. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਰਾਮ ਹਰਿ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗੁਰ ਲਿਵ ਮੀਠਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: raam har keeratan gur liv meeThaa ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Lovingly focused upon the Guru, the Kirtan of the Lord's Praise has become sweet to me. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਅਗਮੁ ਅਗੋਚਰੁ ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਲਾਗਿ ਬਸੀਠਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: har agam agochar paarabraham hai mil satigur laag baseeThaa ||
lines.translation: The Lord, the Supreme Lord God, is Inaccessible and Unfathomable. Those who are committed to the True Guru, the Divine Intermediary, meet the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨ ਗੁਰ ਬਚਨ ਸੁਖਾਨੇ ਹੀਅਰੈ ਤਿਨ ਆਗੈ ਆਣਿ ਪਰੀਠਾ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: jin gur bachan sukhaane heearai tin aagai aan pareeThaa ||2||
lines.translation: Those whose hearts are pleased with the Guru's Teachings - the Lord's Presence is revealed to them. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨਮੁਖ ਹੀਅਰਾ ਅਤਿ ਕਠੋਰੁ ਹੈ ਤਿਨ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਕਾਰ ਕਰੀਠਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: manmukh heearaa at kaThor hai tin a(n)tar kaar kareeThaa ||
lines.translation: The hearts of the self-willed manmukhs are hard and cruel; their inner beings are dark.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਸੀਅਰ ਕਉ ਬਹੁ ਦੂਧੁ ਪੀਆਈਐ ਬਿਖੁ ਨਿਕਸੈ ਫੋਲਿ ਫੁਲੀਠਾ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: biseear kau bahu dhoodh peeaaieeaai bikh nikasai fol fuleeThaa ||3||
lines.translation: Even if the poisonous snake is fed large amounts of milk, it will still yield only poison. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨਿ ਮਿਲਾਵਹੁ ਗੁਰੁ ਸਾਧੂ ਘਸਿ ਗਰੁੜੁ ਸਬਦੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਲੀਠਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: har prabh aan milaavahu gur saadhoo ghas garuR sabadh mukh leeThaa ||
lines.translation: O Lord God, please unite me with the Holy Guru, so that I might joyfully grind and eat the Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਲਾਲੇ ਗੋਲੇ ਲਗਿ ਸੰਗਤਿ ਕਰੂਆ ਮੀਠਾ ॥੪॥੯॥੨੩॥੬੧॥
lines.transliteration: jan naanak gur ke laale gole lag sa(n)gat karooaa meeThaa ||4||9||23||61||
lines.translation: Servant Nanak is the slave of the Guru; in the Sangat, the Holy Congregation, the bitter becomes sweet. ||4||9||23||61||

structure: The shabad begins by exposing the tragedy of living near the treasure without tasting it.
From there it contrasts the sweetness given through Guru and Shabad with the poison of the hard heart.
The closing movement rests in prayer for union, Sangat, and the miracle of bitterness becoming sweet.
